data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Investors who prefer to own the whole market can use the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which holds about US$11.9 billion in assets.

Last week was a reminder of how quickly the math can change. The TAIEX fell 4.6%, its first weekly decline in five weeks, as a technology selloff spread and TSMC CEO C.C. Wei warned of macroeconomic uncertainty and weak consumer demand, according to Trading Economics. In New York, TSMC's shares fell 8.98% from the Oct. 9 close to $412.61 on Oct. 16, ASE dropped 14.86% to $39.53, UMC slid 13.68% to $19.82, the iShares fund lost 7.04% to $106.26 and The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ) declined 8.78% to $94.18, according to Stock Analysis data. For the managers who just traded a salary for their own account, those swings now land on them.

data.title: Sophia Space Deploys Orbital Computing Software Across Multiple Kepler Satellites
data.description:
First in-space deployment of Sophia Orbital Operating System (SOOS) aboard multiple Kepler Communications satellites opens the door for organizations to run workloads in orbit and accelerate the future of scalable orbital data centers.

PASADENA, Calif., Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Sophia Space, a pioneer in passively-cooled orbital computing infrastructure, today announced the first in-space deployment of its Sophia Orbital Operating System (SOOS) leveraging the on-orbit compute infrastructure aboard multiple Kepler satellites within Kepler's Tranche 1 optical data relay constellation. The collaboration is advancing the company's effort to deploy scalable computing infrastructure in orbit. This deployment establishes a foundational software layer for Sophia Space's future orbital computing architecture, designed to support computing workloads across individual spacecraft and larger, distributed orbital networks.

Sophia Space deploys SOOS across multiple Kepler satellites, paving the way for scalable orbital data centers.

Hosted aboard Kepler satellites, the SOOS deployment validates resilient, autonomous software capabilities needed to manage and execute distributed edge computing workloads across multiple spacecraft connected via optical links in the space environment. This software demonstration marks an important step toward dedicated orbital computing infrastructure capable of processing mission-critical data in space, enabling faster insights, greater operational resilience, and more sophisticated space-based data services.

"Building the next generation of space infrastructure isn't about launching an entire data center overnight. It's about proving the architecture, step by step," said Rob DeMillo, CEO and Co-Founder of Sophia Space. "Deploying SOOS in LEO is an important first step. We're beginning with the software foundation, then moving toward dedicated computing hardware, standalone satellites, and ultimately entire constellations. Each mission builds toward a future where computing becomes an integral part of the orbital economy."

The collaboration also highlights the growing convergence of satellite communications and orbital computing, creating opportunities to run AI inference workloads closer to where data is collected and generated. SOOS enables distributed edge computing through managed Kubernetes application deployment and management; software that runs and manages applications across a group of computers. SOOS offers triple redundancy and built-in security capabilities designed to support resilient operations for partners looking to deploy AI inference workloads in orbit across a variety of applications, including missile warning, space domain awareness, maritime awareness, disaster response, atmospheric monitoring and weather intelligence, spacecraft operations, zero-gravity manufacturing, and a host of other potential uses.

"As the space economy grows, communications and computing will become increasingly interconnected," said Caitlin Marsh, president of Kepler US. "Our collaboration with Sophia Space reflects the importance of building an orbital infrastructure ecosystem where data can be processed, managed, and delivered more efficiently. This is an early step toward demonstrating how those capabilities can work together."

SOOS deployment represents the first step in Sophia Space's broader development roadmap, designed to progressively validate the technologies needed to deliver scalable computing infrastructure in orbit. Sophia Space is now open to partner with other companies looking to deploy edge applications in LEO. 

"I want to congratulate the software and operations teams at Sophia Space and Kepler for successfully demonstrating distributed operating system functions across multiple satellites in space and multiple GPUs on each satellite," added Dr. Leon Alkalai, Founder and CTO of Sophia Space. "The Sophia team demonstrated distributed functions essential for satellite system resilience, self-awareness and fault tolerance. These building blocks are essential for any future orbiting data centers infrastructure."

These missions are intended to demonstrate how modular computing infrastructure can scale into distributed orbital networks, while advancing opportunities to work with partners to bring new computing capabilities in orbit.

About Sophia Space

Sophia Space is developing the next generation of orbital computing infrastructure through its modular, passively cooled TILE architecture and Sophia Orbital Operating System (SOOS). Drawing on patented, thermal-management innovations originating at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory and the California Institute of Technology, the company is working to make high-performance computing in space more scalable, efficient, and accessible. Headquartered in Pasadena, California, Sophia Space is building the infrastructure to support a growing space-based economy.

About Kepler Communications

 Kepler Communications Inc. is a space infrastructure provider on a mission to deliver real-time access to space data. With 33 satellites launched to date, Kepler operates the first commercial optical data relay constellation, enabling real-time, continuous space connectivity while supporting advanced on-orbit compute and hosted payload capabilities. Kepler has achieved industry-leading milestones, including the first commercial on-orbit demonstration of SDA-compatible optical inter-satellite links and successful space-to-air and space-to-ground optical communication demonstrations. Headquartered in Toronto, Canada, Kepler is building a global company to enable the future space economy.

data.title: MORNING BID EUROPE-Loading ... Claude and GTA VI
data.description:
Nov 19 (Reuters) - A look at the day ahead in European and global markets from Ankur Banerjee

The latest test of how investors feel about the AI trade is here as Claude chatbot maker Anthropic gets ready for its market debut after clinching an eye-watering $1.5 trillion valuation in the biggest-ever initial public offering.

Anthropic is the first major frontier AI model developer to go public and priced its IPO at $83 apiece, raising $81 billion to claim the title of the largest stock-market debut on record.

Investors say demand is robust for the offering, suggesting a strong opening day, though Asian equities are not basking in the afterglow. Worries about AI profitability and the massive debt-fuelled spending to build related infrastructure have dented sentiment for weeks and Thursday was no different in Asia.

US stock futures, though, pointed higher on the IPO pricing while European stocks were set for a strong opening, suggesting Asia's place as the epicentre of the AI boom has meant it is also feeling the pain much more.

Taiwan's stock market is where most of the action is this week, with the benchmark index down 3.4%, on pace for a weekly decline of 11%. South Korea's KOSPI was flat, set for a 4% weekly fall.

Hawkish comments from the Federal Reserve also cast a shadow over Asian markets, with traders bracing for a hike next month. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said if the central bank wanted to get inflation down, it needed to take more "aggressive action." Traders are pricing in a 10% chance of a 50-basis-point hike, the CME FedWatch tool showed.

That left the dollar standing tall at an 18-month high against major rivals. The yen remains perilously close to the 160-per-dollar mark, leaving traders jittery about intervention. The Asian currency is down 1.8% so far in 2026 as authorities in Tokyo stepped in to support the yen in several bouts of intervention earlier this year.

Anthropic's debut is not the only eagerly awaited event on Thursday, with "Grand Theft Auto VI" rolling out across the globe after 13 years and an estimated $1 billion or more in production costs. Early reviews for the game, which could bring in billions of dollars for its developer, Take-Two Interactive studio Rockstar Games, are euphoric.

Key developments that could influence markets on Thursday:

Anthropic market debut, Walmart earnings, GTA VI debut

(Reporting by Ankur Banerjee in Singapore; Editing by Thomas Derpinghaus)

data.title: JBIC chair calls for greater Japanese role in $550 billion US investment
data.description:
TOKYO, Nov 19 (Reuters) - The chair of state-owned Japan Bank for International Cooperation (JBIC) said on Thursday he is seeking a greater Japanese role in selecting projects under a $550 billion investment initiative in the United States.

JBIC is at the centre of Japan's commitment to invest up to $550 billion in US projects, providing financing for projects selected under the initiative agreed last year as part of a deal that lowered US tariffs on Japanese imports to 15%.

"Ideally, I would like the framework to be revised so that Japan can participate in the origination of projects," JBIC chair Tadashi Maeda told Reuters in an interview on the sidelines of the Raisina Tokyo dialogue, a Japan-India forum held in Tokyo.

Under the framework agreed by Washington and Tokyo last year, the US identifies projects eligible for the initiative, while the Japanese side participates in consultations and assesses whether individual projects qualify for financing.

JBIC has used consultations on individual investments to push for terms that better reflect Japanese interests, Maeda said, arguing that Japan's direct involvement would help improve the selection process.

The two governments have so far announced seven projects worth more than $100 billion under the initiative, including a semiconductor manufacturing project by GlobalFoundries in New York and power generation projects in Texas and Ohio.

Separately, Maeda said JBIC sees India's nascent semiconductor industry as an important pillar of efforts to diversify global supply chains away from China and reduce risks associated with the concentration of advanced chip production in Taiwan.

JBIC has had a front-row seat to India's semiconductor ambitions through its 2013 acquisition of a 26% stake in National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation (NICDC), a government-backed company that builds industrial zones across India.

NICDC has helped develop industrial zones including Dholera in Gujarat state, which has since become the centrepiece of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's drive to build a domestic chip industry.

"One way of looking at this is to build a supply chain that is separate from a specific country, namely China," Maeda said.

He noted India remained in the early stages of developing a semiconductor ecosystem but its rapid economic growth, a young talent pool and policy continuity under Modi made it an attractive long-term partner for Japan.

India is likely to become an extremely important player both as a market and as part of the supply chain, he said. "Japan needs to work with India from a long-term perspective to build a supply chain that covers the entire ecosystem," he said.

(Reporting by Makiko Yamazaki and Tamiyuki Kihara; Editing by Sam Holmes)

data.title: Global Electronics Association: Growing Shortages Across the PCB Supply Chain Threaten the Next Wave of AI and Electronics
data.description:
Bannockburn, Illinois, USA, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- The Global Electronics Association, the voice of the electronics industry, is issuing this Industry Alert on escalating shortages across the printed circuit board (PCB) supply chain. Companies in automotive, industrial, medical, defense, and telecommunications report longer lead times and difficulty securing supply as AI absorbs scarce capacity, effectively putting production at risk. Availability, not price, is the real risk facing the industry and outlined in the Explanatory Report, “PCB Squeeze: A Wake-Up Call for Global Electronics.”

The Demand Shift

  ·While demand is arriving at a scale the supply chain was not built for, it is also coming in its most material-intensive form.

  • A typical PC board has about 12 layers, while AI-server boards are moving to 40-60+ layers, and every added layer draws more glass fabric, resin, copper foil, and laminate.
  • Bookings rose 56.1% in the year to September while shipments rose 13.3%, and lead times for high-layer boards run 16–20 weeks or more, according to Association data.
  • Unprecedented demand is straining both board fabrication and the materials needed to support it, with each constraint compounding the next.

Why New Capacity Isn’t Enough

  • Asia makes more than 90% of the world’s boards: a range of industry estimates confirm that no less than $10 billion USD has gone into new PCB plants in Southeast Asia; and at least as much has been invested in China over the past three years.
  • Still, supply is not keeping pace. Fabrication capacity is expanding, but new lines depend on glass fabric, resin, copper foil, and laminate; materials that are themselves constrained. More board capacity alone cannot resolve the shortage.
  • Other regions face the same global squeeze with a much smaller manufacturing footprint. In Europe, for example, the share of global PCB production fell from 13.8% in 2000 to 2.2% in 2023. 

Outlook: Through 2027 and Beyond

  • Against this backdrop, strong demand, increasing complexity, and slower capacity additions across the supply chain will keep the PCB shortage going through at least the first half of 2027. Meaningful relief is unlikely before mid-2028.
  • In the meantime, hyperscalers, the largest buyers, are locking up what supply there is, and automotive, industrial, medical, and defense customers are falling to the back of the queue.

Why It Matters

  • The consequences reach well beyond the PCB industry. Every electronic system runs on PCBs, so investments in semiconductors and final assembly can’t deliver results without the boards and materials that connect them.
  • This level of supply chain exposure, in the Association’s assessment, may very well rival the 2021 chip shortage. 

Recommendations for Manufacturers

Manufacturers should work closely with their customers and suppliers to share realistic demand forecasts, avoid double-booking, and qualify alternate sources for laminate, prepreg, and foil.

Recommendations for Governments

Governments should treat PCB supply disruption as an urgent strategic risk. The Association urges governments to:

  1. Early warning. Establish a channel with industry to track PCB and PCB materials lead times
  2. Fund the whole stack. Extend semiconductor incentives, including tax incentives for investment in new equipment, to advanced PCB and substrate fabrication.
  3. Faster permitting. Accelerate permitting for new capacity.
  4. New materials. Invest in R&D and in the qualification of new alternative materials, including funding for the testing and customer approval that determine how quickly alternatives can enter supply.

data.title: JBIC chair calls for greater Japanese role in $550 billion US investment
data.description:
TOKYO, Nov 19 (Reuters) - The chair of state-owned Japan Bank for International Cooperation (JBIC) said on Thursday he is seeking a greater Japanese role in selecting projects under a $550 billion investment initiative in the United States.

JBIC is at the centre of Japan's commitment to invest up to $550 billion in US projects, providing financing for projects selected under the initiative agreed last year as part of a deal that lowered US tariffs on Japanese imports to 15%.

"Ideally, I would like the framework to be revised so that Japan can participate in the origination of projects," JBIC chair Tadashi Maeda told Reuters in an interview on the sidelines of the Raisina Tokyo dialogue, a Japan-India forum held in Tokyo.

Under the framework agreed by Washington and Tokyo last year, the US identifies projects eligible for the initiative, while the Japanese side participates in consultations and assesses whether individual projects qualify for financing.

JBIC has used consultations on individual investments to push for terms that better reflect Japanese interests, Maeda said, arguing that Japan's direct involvement would help improve the selection process.

The two governments have so far announced seven projects worth more than $100 billion under the initiative, including a semiconductor manufacturing project by GlobalFoundries in New York and power generation projects in Texas and Ohio.

Separately, Maeda said JBIC sees India's nascent semiconductor industry as an important pillar of efforts to diversify global supply chains away from China and reduce risks associated with the concentration of advanced chip production in Taiwan.

JBIC has had a front-row seat to India's semiconductor ambitions through its 2013 acquisition of a 26% stake in National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation (NICDC), a government-backed company that builds industrial zones across India.

NICDC has helped develop industrial zones including Dholera in Gujarat state, which has since become the centrepiece of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's drive to build a domestic chip industry.

"One way of looking at this is to build a supply chain that is separate from a specific country, namely China," Maeda said.

He noted India remained in the early stages of developing a semiconductor ecosystem but its rapid economic growth, a young talent pool and policy continuity under Modi made it an attractive long-term partner for Japan.

India is likely to become an extremely important player both as a market and as part of the supply chain, he said. "Japan needs to work with India from a long-term perspective to build a supply chain that covers the entire ecosystem," he said.

data.title: Grand Theft Auto VI draws rave reviews as gamers enter Vice City
data.description:
By Aditya Soni and Cordelia Hsu

SYDNEY, Nov 19 (Reuters) - After 13 years and an estimated $1 billion or more in production costs, "Grand Theft Auto VI" rolled out across the globe on Thursday, gaining rapturous early reviews for the most anticipated video game release in history.

The game, which could bring in billions of dollars for its developer, Take-Two Interactive studio Rockstar Games, raced to the top of Metacritic's all-time gaming leaderboard with a score of 99, a mark matched by only one other title, Nintendo's 1998 classic "The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time".

The game went online as midnight struck in New Zealand, with launches worldwide following the clock through Thursday.

"It is the best game that's ever been made and we're only 20 minutes deep," said 33-year-old Asif Mir as he started to play and livestream just after midnight in Sydney, one of the first places where the game was unlocked.

In London, gamers counted down to the release at parties across the city.

"Today has been a day that I have waited for my whole life," said 20-year-old influencer Archie Whitby.

"To be living it, it feels almost dystopian. It doesn't feel real."

Miami, the inspiration for the game's fictional Vice City setting, was one of the last places to get in on the action.

The city's NBA team, the Miami Heat, celebrated the release with a Vice City-themed match against the Milwaukee Bucks, with the court and stadium adorned with the game's colours of neon pink and blue.

Millions of players have already downloaded the game to their consoles, with many expected to take time off work - or call in sick - to play the latest installment in a franchise that since its 1997 debut has become one of the best-selling video game series of all time.

"It's the Star Wars of this generation," said Joost van Dreunen, adjunct professor at NYU Stern School of Business.

"It's a synchronized, shared event. So millions of people will all want to be there the first couple of days, the first few weeks of experiencing it as it goes live."

Strong initial reviews of the game - available on Sony's PlayStation 5 and Microsoft's Xbox Series X and ​S consoles - helped push up Take-Two Interactive's US shares by 6.5% on Wednesday afternoon in New York.

'TRULY ASTONISHING': GAME GETS STRONG USER REVIEWS

The original "Grand Theft Auto" looks basic by today's standards, with a storyline - stealing cars and carrying out jobs for ​crime syndicates - that angered politicians and parents, even as it delighted fans.

But as the series progressed it became increasingly sophisticated, mixing its trademark crime, driving and morally dubious missions with activities ranging from parachute jumps to cinema visits and radio stations satirizing US culture.

"Grand Theft Auto V", released in 2013, was set in the fictional Los Santos, a stand-in for Los Angeles. The action now moves to Vice City, a fictional version of Miami, in the state of Leonida, the game's take on Florida.

Play will switch between two leading characters, Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval. They are partners in crime and romantically involved - just how romantically will be up to the player. There will be nightclubs, gun stores, scuba diving and a zoo. But much remains to be revealed.

GTA VI could prove less provocative than its predecessors, said Tore Olsson, a professor at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville, who teaches a course on US history since 1980 through the GTA games. The game sits more within mainstream culture now and its promotional materials suggest it will reward more ethical play styles, he said.

"There's no doubt that Jason and Lucia of VI will be criminals, and they'll be regularly breaking the law. But I don't think the new game will require players to enact wanton slaughter, and it may indeed penalize those who choose to play that way," said Olsson.

Having Lucia as one of the two lead characters should help address complaints about a lack of playable female characters in previous iterations of GTA. Women will be an estimated 4 out of 10 GTA VI players in the US, according to a Bain survey.

Analytics firm Sensor Tower estimated that so far over 17 million copies have been sold for more than $1.65 billion.

With so much anticipation, the risk of disappointment is high. Play that is perceived as too easy or too hard, an unsatisfying storyline, or significant bugs and glitches at launch can all affect a game's reputation and future sales.

With the main part of the game estimated to take around 50 hours to complete, full reactions were not available immediately. But initial reviews from gaming industry experts were almost universal in their high praise.

Entertainment website GamesRadar+ said Rockstar had built a world of "truly astonishing scale, scope, and quality". This release "will be talked about for years to come" and was "well worth the 13-year wait," said PC Games. Various outlets called it a "masterpiece."

Some gamers in the US awaiting their turn were unnerved when the PlayStation Network was hit by a temporary outage on Wednesday afternoon, but service was soon restored.

While some economists have warned about lost productivity as gamers take time off from work, consumer analysts said the economy could also receive a boost from sales of the game, consoles, storage upgrades, and even food delivery services.

Luke Maxwell, a 27-year-old father of two who works in sales on Australia's ​Gold Coast, was one of those who booked time off work to play. "I've already told the whole family, don't bother me, don't talk to me," he said.

(Additional reporting by Rosalba O'Brien in New York, Matt Silverstein in Los Angeles, Adrianna Ebert in Gdansk and Christine Chen in Sydney; Writing by Rosalba O'Brien, Adam Jourdan and Alasdair Pal; Editing by Daniel Wallis, Kate Mayberry, Mark Potter and Catherine Evans)

data.title: Anthropic raises record $81 billion in IPO at $1.5 trillion valuation
data.description:
Nov 18 (Reuters) - Anthropic has raised $81.3 billion in the largest stock-market debut on record after upsizing its offering, valuing the Claude chatbot maker at $1.5 trillion in a deal that defies concerns about the AI trade and tech fundraising prospects.

The first major frontier AI model developer to go public, Anthropic on Wednesday priced its shares at $83 apiece, above its initial range of $70 to $78, in a sign of strong demand for the shares from investors.

Reuters was first to report earlier on Wednesday that the company increased the number of shares it was selling by about 19% to 980 million shares. The upsized IPO eclipsed the previous record-setting debut of Elon Musk's SpaceX in June.

The total deal size is $107.3 billion, including another $26 billion Anthropic is raising through a private placement of shares at the IPO price, the filings showed.

Anthropic comes to the public market even as the backdrop for AI stocks has turned challenging.

In recent weeks chipmakers and cloud companies, which have raised hundreds of billions of dollars to fund their massive spending plans, have come under pressure due to valuation concerns, mounting AI infrastructure costs and the sudden exit of Nvidia's ( NVDA ) Jensen Huang, a pillar of the industry's growth.

At the same time, Anthropic has faced questions about its outlook and ability to sustain rapid growth as competition in the industry intensifies.

Armina Rosenberg, portfolio manager and co-founder of Minotaur Capital, which is awaiting an Anthropic share allocation, said the company's IPO was a useful gauge of investor appetite for AI.

"But one listing won't settle the debate. There's a genuine wall of worry right now, and it'll take a few things to climb it. Once Anthropic reports publicly, it becomes one of the clearest tests of whether the economics of AI are holding up," she said.

On a fully diluted basis, the IPO now values the company at about $1.5 trillion, including securities such as stock options and restricted stock. On a non-diluted basis, the valuation stands at about $1.1 trillion.

US stock futures were up after Anthropic's IPO details were made public, while Asian tech stocks remained under pressure amid broader concerns about the AI trade. Anthropic is set to start trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker ANT.

A strong debut could give confidence to other companies waiting to tap public markets. Anthropic's closest rival, OpenAI, is expected to pursue a listing as early as next year.

Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley ( MS ) are the lead underwriters for Anthropic's offering, which has a 22-bank underwriting syndicate. The two banks also served as lead underwriters for SpaceX's IPO earlier this year. 

SPENDING COMMITMENTS EXPOSE RISKS

Anthropic's growth has been driven by surging demand for its Claude models, particularly Claude Code, its coding agent that has gained popularity among software developers. Its annualized revenue run rate reached $81 billion as of October 31, up $10 billion from September 30, according to its IPO filing.

The Claude maker said it had 11,900 customers generating at least $100,000 in annual revenue on a trailing 12-month basis as of September 30, compared with more than 1,500 at the end of last year, underscoring its growing business foothold.

But sustaining that growth is becoming expensive. Anthropic spent nearly $9 billion on computing capacity and infrastructure in the first half of 2026, nearly four times the amount spent a year earlier.

It also incurred an additional $5 billion in computing costs in the third quarter, reducing the revenue generated per dollar of computing capacity.

Revenue rose 47% in the third quarter to $16.96 billion from the second quarter. The company reported an operating loss of $567 million, compared with operating income of $974 million in the previous quarter.

The net loss narrowed to $23.3 billion from $66.3 billion a quarter earlier, including non-operating ​items related to bonds convertible into its shares. 

Anthropic has committed to nearly $900 billion in computing spending with infrastructure partners, including Amazon ( AMZN ) and Alphabet's Google, to train and operate AI models.

It warned that its computing providers and infrastructure partners depend on third-party financing and credit support to acquire chips and build capacity. 

"If such financing or support becomes unavailable or more costly, contracted capacity may be delayed, repriced, reduced, or not delivered," Anthropic said in an IPO filing. 

COMPETITION AND SAFETY CHALLENGES

Anthropic faces questions over how it will balance its commercial ambitions with its emphasis on AI safety.

CEO Dario Amodei has called for the industry to slow the pace of developing and releasing increasingly powerful models, warning that advances in AI could outstrip society's ability to manage the risks.

"Our development of highly advanced models, platforms, and applications and expansion of use cases could further increase the risk that our models cause harm," Anthropic said in the filing.

At the same time, competition is intensifying against Anthropic to be the leading provider of AI tools for businesses.

OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra, its latest flagship AI model, accounted for about 13% of enterprise AI spending tracked by corporate expense platform Ramp, compared with about 8% for Anthropic's Claude Fable, according to data cited by Reuters in September.

The competitive threat extends beyond the handful of companies developing the most powerful commercial models. A recent Capgemini study found that 59% of executives at large companies plan to increase their use of open-weight models over the next year as AI costs exceed budgets.

Meta Platforms ( META ), one of Anthropic's largest customers, has been looking to reduce its use of the startup's models as it develops more AI capabilities internally, Reuters previously reported.

"Our thesis is that the vast amount of value will accrue to whoever is at the frontier," said Peter Singlehurst, head of private companies at Baillie Gifford, which invested roughly $1.5 billion in Anthropic before its IPO.

"Our bet is that Anthropic has the ingredients - that doesn't guarantee, but means that they arguably have the highest probability of remaining at the frontier."

(Reporting by Echo Wang in New York; additional reporting by Ankur Banerjee in Singapore; Editing by David Gaffen, Christian Plumb, Matthew Lewis and Sonali Paul)

Armina Rosenberg, portfolio manager and co-founder of Minotaur Capital, which is awaiting an Anthropic share allocation, said the company's IPO was a useful gauge of investor appetite for AI.

"But one listing won't settle the debate. There's a genuine wall of worry right now, and it'll take a few things to climb it. Once Anthropic reports publicly, it becomes one of the clearest tests of whether the economics of AI are holding up," she said.

On a fully diluted basis, the IPO now values the company at about $1.5 trillion, including securities such as stock options and restricted stock. On a non-diluted basis, the valuation stands at about $1.1 trillion.

US stock futures were up after Anthropic's IPO details were made public, while Asian tech stocks remained under pressure amid broader concerns about the AI trade. Anthropic is set to start trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker ANT.

A strong debut could give confidence to other companies waiting to tap public markets. Anthropic's closest rival, OpenAI, is expected to pursue a listing as early as next year.

Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley ( MS ) are the lead underwriters for Anthropic's offering, which has a 22-bank underwriting syndicate. The two banks also served as lead underwriters for SpaceX's IPO earlier this year. 

SPENDING COMMITMENTS EXPOSE RISKS

Anthropic's growth has been driven by surging demand for its Claude models, particularly Claude Code, its coding agent that has gained popularity among software developers. Its annualized revenue run rate reached $81 billion as of October 31, up $10 billion from September 30, according to its IPO filing.

The Claude maker said it had 11,900 customers generating at least $100,000 in annual revenue on a trailing 12-month basis as of September 30, compared with more than 1,500 at the end of last year, underscoring its growing business foothold.

But sustaining that growth is becoming expensive. Anthropic spent nearly $9 billion on computing capacity and infrastructure in the first half of 2026, nearly four times the amount spent a year earlier.

It also incurred an additional $5 billion in computing costs in the third quarter, reducing the revenue generated per dollar of computing capacity.

Revenue rose 47% in the third quarter to $16.96 billion from the second quarter. The company reported an operating loss of $567 million, compared with operating income of $974 million in the previous quarter.

The net loss narrowed to $23.3 billion from $66.3 billion a quarter earlier, including non-operating ​items related to bonds convertible into its shares. 

Anthropic has committed to nearly $900 billion in computing spending with infrastructure partners, including Amazon ( AMZN ) and Alphabet's Google, to train and operate AI models.

It warned that its computing providers and infrastructure partners depend on third-party financing and credit support to acquire chips and build capacity. 

"If such financing or support becomes unavailable or more costly, contracted capacity may be delayed, repriced, reduced, or not delivered," Anthropic said in an IPO filing. 

COMPETITION AND SAFETY CHALLENGES

Anthropic faces questions over how it will balance its commercial ambitions with its emphasis on AI safety.

CEO Dario Amodei has called for the industry to slow the pace of developing and releasing increasingly powerful models, warning that advances in AI could outstrip society's ability to manage the risks.

"Our development of highly advanced models, platforms, and applications and expansion of use cases could further increase the risk that our models cause harm," Anthropic said in the filing.

At the same time, competition is intensifying against Anthropic to be the leading provider of AI tools for businesses.

OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra, its latest flagship AI model, accounted for about 13% of enterprise AI spending tracked by corporate expense platform Ramp, compared with about 8% for Anthropic's Claude Fable, according to data cited by Reuters in September.

The competitive threat extends beyond the handful of companies developing the most powerful commercial models. A recent Capgemini study found that 59% of executives at large companies plan to increase their use of open-weight models over the next year as AI costs exceed budgets.

Meta Platforms, one of Anthropic's largest customers, has been looking to reduce its use of the startup's models as it develops more AI capabilities internally, Reuters previously reported.

"Our thesis is that the vast amount of value will accrue to whoever is at the frontier," said Peter Singlehurst, head of private companies at Baillie Gifford, which invested roughly $1.5 billion in Anthropic before its IPO.

"Our bet is that Anthropic has the ingredients - that doesn't guarantee, but means that they arguably have the highest probability of remaining at the frontier."

(Reporting by Echo Wang in New York; additional reporting by Ankur Banerjee in Singapore; Editing by David Gaffen, Christian Plumb, Matthew Lewis and Sonali Paul)

data.title: 'GTA VI' to supercharge Sony - just not in Japan
data.description:
TOKYO, Nov 19 (Reuters) - The global launch of "Grand Theft Auto VI" on Thursday is expected to provide a major boost to PlayStation maker Sony -- albeit not in its home market of Japan, where the franchise is a niche pursuit.

The long-awaited open-world crime action game from Take-Two Interactive's Rockstar Games is rolling out across the world and has been met with rave reviews and fans taking time off work to play.

Three-quarters of the 17 million "GTA VI" units sold are on PlayStation, according to estimates from Sensor Tower, outselling Xbox maker Microsoft ( MSFT ).

Shares in Sony, whose PlayStation 5 console is in its seventh year on the market, were up almost 3% in Tokyo compared with flat trading in the benchmark index.

Analysts think that momentum is unlikely to extend to Japan, where Switch 2 maker Nintendo ( NTDOF ) dominates the gaming device market and consumers prefer anime-style titles to realistic, violent Western games.

"The current trends in Japan don't really fit this kind of game," said Toyo Securities analyst Hideki Yasuda.

"It won't sell much in Japan, but there's absolutely no need for this game to sell in Japan," he said.

Earlier this year Sony scored a major global success with movie "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" but in Japan faced competition from breakout hit "Chiikawa the Movie: The Secret of Mermaid Island."

"A few of my friends bought 'GTA VI' at midnight but I'm in no hurry to as it's only on PS5 and Xbox and you can't play multiplayer online yet," said Sorataka Goto, 33, who was shopping in Tokyo's Akihabara electronics district.

"If and when it's on PC and you can play online I'll consider buying it," said Goto, who bought the remake of the "The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time".

Nintendo ( NTDOF ) has sold more than five million copies of the Switch 2 title, which was originally on the Nintendo ( NTDOF ) 64, in the first four days since its launch earlier this month.

"I had the original as a child and so was excited to try this version," he said.

SONY FACING PROCUREMENT HEADWINDS

Analysts expect the release of "GTA VI" to soften the decline of PS5 hardware sales this year and support growth in software sales.

Sony sold 2.6 million PS5 units during the July to September quarter, which analysts see as reflecting demand ahead of "GTA VI", down from 4 million a year earlier.

"We've modeled PlayStation profits materially ahead of the Street in the next couple of quarters, on account of the 'GTA VI' launch," Bernstein analyst David Dai wrote in a note.

The release is bolstering Sony's ( SONY ) games slate after it delayed the launch of "God of War Laufey" by three months to May 2027.

Sony is grappling with procurement challenges as the cost of memory chips has risen sharply due to the AI boom.

"I don't get the sense that Sony has much desire to aggressively sell hardware... the benefits Sony gets from royalties will be enormous," said Toyo Securities' Yasuda.

(Reporting by Sam Nussey and Kentaro Okasaka; Editing by Kate Mayberry)

data.title: LGS Lab Gas System Launches Next Generation Ultra High Purity Laboratory Gas Delivery System Solutions
data.description:
SHANGHAI, CN / ACCESS Newswire / November 18, 2026 / LGS Lab Gas System, a leading manufacturer and engineering contractor of ultra high purity gas delivery equipment, today announced its expanded suite of centralized laboratory gas supply systems and precision fluid handling components. Designed to meet the rigorous demands of semiconductor fabrication, pharmaceutical development, biotechnology, and analytical testing, the integrated product line ensures stable pressure control and parts per billion purity from central storage rooms to point of use instruments.

Modern analytical instruments such as gas chromatographs and mass spectrometers require uninterrupted, contamination free gas streams to produce accurate and repeatable results. Traditional cylinder setups located directly inside work areas create safety risks, consume valuable floor space, and introduce pressure fluctuations during manual tank replacements. LGS Lab Gas System eliminates these operational challenges by moving gas sources into dedicated exterior or isolated rooms and delivering media through continuous, orbital welded stainless steel pipelines.

The company portfolio covers every critical stage of gas management. At the source level, LGS provides fully automatic and semi automatic specialty gas cabinets, including the JW 300 GC and JW 200 GC models. Built with exhausted, explosion proof enclosures, programmable logic controller purge sequences, and ten inch touchscreens, these cabinets safely manage hazardous, toxic, and corrosive media such as silane, ammonia, hydrogen chloride, and nitrogen trifluoride. Automatic changeover manifolds monitor cylinder pressure in real time and switch seamlessly between primary and reserve banks without interrupting downstream operations.

For distribution and final delivery, LGS manufactures electropolished 316L and VIM VAR stainless steel tubing, valve manifold boxes, packless metal diaphragm valves, ultra high purity pressure regulators, and point of use outlet panels. Every wetted component undergoes strict surface finishing and cleaning to prevent outgassing, particle generation, and moisture ingress. Integrated gas leak detectors, excess flow switches, and emergency shutoff valves work together to protect personnel and facility assets around the clock.

Beyond component manufacturing, LGS Lab Gas System delivers complete turnkey engineering services. Experienced project teams support clients from initial site assessment and pipeline layout design through clean room assembly, automated orbital welding, helium leak testing, and final certification documentation. By combining matched hardware with certified installation practices, LGS helps laboratories achieve compliance with international safety codes while lowering long term maintenance costs.

About LGS Lab Gas System

Headquartered in Songjiang District, Shanghai, LGS Lab Gas System specializes in the design, production, and installation of ultra high purity laboratory gas systems and specialty gas equipment. Serving research institutions, universities, semiconductor plants, and life science laboratories worldwide, the company is dedicated to advancing laboratory safety, gas purity, and operational reliability.

data.title: Linq Raises $90 Million in New Funding Led by Andreessen Horowitz to Build the Infrastructure Platform for AI Agents
data.description:
Every business and every person will have an agent. With more than 1 billion messages processed, Linq is building the infrastructure to put them to work.

SAN FRANCISCO, Nov. 18, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Linq, the infrastructure platform for AI agents, today announced $90 million in new funding led by Andreessen Horowitz, with continued participation from TQ Ventures, Mucker Capital, and Abstract, and new participation from Anthos and Left Lane Capital. Ben Horowitz will join its board of directors.

The internet gave every business a website. The iPhone gave every business an app. Now AI is giving every business, and every person, an agent. Cloudflare reports that more than half of internet traffic is no longer human, with AI agent requests on its network up more than 1,700% in a year. These are not simple, customer-service chatbots: these agents book, buy, and make plans by communicating with people and using software on their behalf.

Messaging was Linq's first product and remains a core part of its growing AI infrastructure platform. As the provider for DoorDash, Town, Tomo, and hundreds of others, Linq has already processed more than 1 billion messages. DoorDash uses Linq to help customers find food, build a cart, and check out in a single thread. And now, as an Apple Messaging Service Provider, Linq can help more enterprises launch and scale customer-facing agents on the same channel.

"The best AI experiences fit naturally into people's lives," said Aryan Shah, Head of AI research at DoorDash. "Linq gives us the messaging infrastructure to bring ordering into a familiar conversation, so customers can go from deciding what they want to placing an order in one thread."

"Agents will communicate and get work done just like people do. Linq gives agents the infrastructure to do both at scale," said Ben Horowitz, cofounder and general partner at Andreessen Horowitz.

Messaging is the beginning of a larger shift: people will describe what they need, and agents will get it done. Linq's computer use offering gives agents access to physical computing infrastructure to interact with software and complete tasks. HD Calling for Agents adds voice calling to the platform. The funding will support continued investment in messaging and the expansion of Linq's product lineup through its own software, hardware infrastructure, and strategic partnerships.

"Clicking through five screens to make a payment will become two words to an agent: 'pay rent,'" said Elliott Potter, CEO of Linq. "We help developers build customer-facing agents that use human tools to do human work."

Companies can learn more at https://linqapp.com/

* Anthropic blockbuster IPO pricing fails to lift Asian stocks

* US stock futures gain in anticipation of the biggest-ever IPO

* Investor worries over AI trade cast shadow

* Hawkish Fed lifts dollar to 19-month high

(Updates to Asia mid-morning)

By Ankur Banerjee

SINGAPORE, Nov 19 (Reuters) - Asian stocks slid on Thursday as fears over the AI trade and hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials left sentiment fragile ahead of an eagerly awaited market debut from Anthropic after the Claude chatbot maker scored the biggest IPO ever.

On a fully diluted basis, the IPO values Anthropic, the first major frontier AI model developer to go public, at about $1.5 trillion and its first-day trading will be scrutinised to gauge investor sentiment on the technology.

Anthropic said the IPO was priced at $83 apiece, above its previously targeted range, raising $81 billion to claim the title of the largest stock-market debut on record.

Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com, said it was going to be a huge test for the markets and it looked poised to be a really bullish listing.

"I don't think it's necessarily going to assuage all the fears about AI," he said. "I think much of that boils down to future investment growth."

Traders' immediate reaction was to push US stock futures higher, with Nasdaq futures up nearly 1% and S&P futures 0.6% higher.

Asian equities, though, fell sharply, led by the three top chipmakers: TSMC, Samsung and SK Hynix ( SKHY ) were all down 2%. That left South Korea's KOSPI down 1% while Taiwanese stocks slid 3.8%.

MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan slumped 1.9%, hitting a seven-month low. The index was set for a decline of nearly 6% for the week, its steepest weekly decline since early March.

Investor confidence in AI has been shaken over the past few weeks on worries about the profitability of the technology and the massive debt needed to fund and build related infrastructure.

Markets mostly shrugged off a strong forecast from chipmaker Nvidia ( NVDA ) this week as uncertainty caused by CEO Jensen Huang's departure last week rattled investors. The company's board dismissed the idea of rehiring Huang.

Armina Rosenberg, portfolio manager and co-founder of Minotaur Capital, said the Anthropic IPO is a useful gauge of investor appetite for AI.

"But one listing won't settle the debate," she said. "There's a genuine wall of worry right now, and it'll take a few things to climb it."

In currencies, the dollar was on the front foot as hawkish comments from US Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller bolstered expectations of a rate hike in December.

The euro was at $1.0978, hovering near its lowest point since April 2025. The Japanese yen was at 157.42 per US dollar and sterling fetched $1.31515.

The dollar index, which measures the greenback against six other currencies, was 0.1% higher at 103.92, a 19-month high.

Waller said on CNBC that if the central bank wanted to get inflation down, it needed to take more "aggressive action" either through a half-point increase at the December meeting, or by using the post-meeting statement to set market expectations for further hikes.

The comments followed hotter-than-expected inflation data last week, leaving markets to brace for a rate hike. Traders are pricing in a 90% chance of a 25-basis-point hike next month, the CME FedWatch tool showed.

"More hawkish Fed pricing has so far offset weakness in technology stocks, keeping the USD supported," OCBC strategists said in a note. "Persistent inflation, further Fed tightening and elevated US yields suggest it is still too early to bet against the USD."

The Australian dollar slipped 0.75% to a 10-month low after soft jobs data cemented the view that Australian rates have likely peaked.

In commodities, oil prices remained under pressure as the growing view that the oil market is turning to a surplus weighed. Brent crude futures were 0.58% lower at $91.47 a barrel, set for a third straight weekly decline.

data.title: 'GTA VI' to supercharge Sony - just not in Japan
data.description:
TOKYO, Nov 19 (Reuters) - The global launch of "Grand Theft Auto VI" on Thursday is expected to provide a major boost to PlayStation maker Sony -- albeit not in its home market of Japan, where the franchise is a niche pursuit.

The long-awaited open-world crime action game from Take-Two Interactive's Rockstar Games is rolling out across the world and has been met with rave reviews and fans taking time off work to play.

Three-quarters of the 17 million "GTA VI" units sold are on PlayStation, according to estimates from Sensor Tower, outselling Xbox maker Microsoft ( MSFT ).

Shares in Sony, whose PlayStation 5 console is in its seventh year on the market, were up 2.8% in Tokyo compared with flat trading in the benchmark index.

Analysts think that momentum is unlikely to extend to Japan, where Switch 2 maker Nintendo ( NTDOF ) dominates the gaming device market and consumers prefer anime-style titles to realistic, violent Western games.

"The current trends in Japan don't really fit this kind of game," said Toyo Securities analyst Hideki Yasuda.

"It won't sell much in Japan, but there's absolutely no need for this game to sell in Japan," he said.

Earlier this year Sony scored a major global success with movie "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" but in Japan faced competition from breakout hit "Chiikawa the Movie: The Secret of Mermaid Island."

Analysts expect the release of "GTA VI" to soften the decline of PS5 hardware sales this year and support growth in software sales.

Sony sold 2.6 million PS5 units during the July to September quarter, which analysts see as reflecting demand ahead of "GTA VI", down from 4 million a year earlier.

"We've modeled PlayStation profits materially ahead of the Street in the next couple of quarters, on account of the 'GTA VI' launch," Bernstein analyst David Dai wrote in a note.

The release is bolstering Sony's ( SONY ) games slate after it delayed the launch of "God of War Laufey" by three months to May 2027.

Sony is grappling with procurement challenges as the cost of memory chips has risen sharply due to the AI boom.

"I don't get the sense that Sony has much desire to aggressively sell hardware... the benefits Sony gets from royalties will be enormous," said Toyo Securities' Yasuda.

(Reporting by Sam Nussey and Kentaro Okasaka; Editing by Kate Mayberry)

data.title: Surge in software patches likely behind recent tech outages; bank regulators on alert
data.description:
* AI tools are helping reveal vulnerabilities in software

* Rubio says patching is "creating short-term disruption"

* US banking regulator plans deep dive into outage, source says

(Writes through with details on banking regulator response)

By AJ Vicens and Nupur Anand

Nov 18 (Reuters) - Recent disruptions to the way people work, access bank accounts and travel are likely linked to corporate efforts to rapidly patch newly discovered software vulnerabilities in the AI age, experts said.

US government officials have sought to reassure the public that the tech outages are not related, with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio telling reporters in Manila this week that company patches - software and operating system updates intended to fix security vulnerabilities - are, at times, "creating short-term disruption in the way the system works."

Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton also told a House of Representatives Homeland Security Committee hearing on worldwide threats Wednesday that there is so far no indication that the tech outages are related.

That said, disruptions to services at JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ) on Monday that also affected other banks drew immediate attention from US banking regulators, who have contacted lenders to ensure incidents are contained and not linked to a cyberattack, two people familiar with the matter said.

One of the people said that Treasury officials also were making inquiries.

The advent of easily accessible AI tools and large language models has supercharged the discovery of vulnerabilities in software. Microsoft ( MSFT ) this month has addressed more than 1,200 software vulnerabilities, nearly 20 times higher than in the same month a year ago, according to cybersecurity firm Qualys ( QLYS ).

"AI has made finding critical vulnerabilities fast and cheap, and the number of flaws that demand immediate patching has grown with it," said Yuval Itzchakov, CTO and co-founder of autonomous offensive security company A Security.

"Emergency patches go into core infrastructure within hours, often without the full testing cycle, and they are intrusive by design: they change runtimes, kernels and network components that everything else depends on. That speed and scale of change is itself a source of failure," Itzchakov said.

Josh Bressers, director of coordinated vulnerability disclosure at cybersecurity firm VulnCheck, said that in 2026 there have been 100,000 publicly disclosed vulnerabilities, tracked by industry as Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures, or CVEs. Of those, Bressers said, 1,363 were known to have been exploited in the real world.

BANK REGULATOR PLANS DEEP DIVE INTO ISSUE

Within the banking sector, at least one major bank was rushing to address a wave of recent patches and there is a lot of work needed, a person at the bank said.

After the outage at JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ), lenders received inquiries from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), according to a separate person, who added that the US banking regulator was trying to assess the impact and wanted to know about communication to customers.

The Treasury and the OCC were calling banks minutes after the incident was reported to check that the issue was contained and it was not a cyber-related incident, a third person said.

The banks were asked to communicate to the customers that they should not panic and that everything was under control, that person said.

The OCC is also going to do a deep dive into the issue and check that everything the regulator was told is correct and that there are no other shortcomings, the person added.

All sources spoke on condition of anonymity.

OCC head Jonathan Gould told an industry event on Tuesday that the JPMorgan ( JPM ) outage was "an isolated incident".

"The OCC, as you would expect, was very involved identifying the issue, talking to the bank in question and talking to the other banks that were affected," he said.

The US Treasury did not respond to a request seeking comment.

Ronald Gestiehr, director of wealth management at Luttner Financial, said technology has made banking "incredibly convenient, and while occasional outages can be frustrating, I don't believe the outages will have a significant impact on consumer confidence or change how most people manage their money."

"Financial institutions have invested heavily in technology and security, and, unfortunately, occasional disruptions will happen," Gestiehr said. "What matters most is how quickly those issues are identified, resolved and communicated to customers."

(Reporting by AJ Vicens in Detroit, Nupur Anand, Stephen Gandal and Saeed Azhar in New York; Editing by Megan Davies, Will Dunham, Diane Craft and Edwina Gibbs)

data.title: Fed policymakers concerned about financial system risks, minutes show
data.description:
NEW YORK, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Financial stability risks tied to aggressive artificial intelligence investment and elevated asset prices are on the US central bank's radar, the minutes from the Federal Reserve's policy meeting last month showed on Wednesday.

The concern was raised as part of a broad review of financial risks by Fed policymakers and central bank staff at the October 27-28 policy meeting. That gathering saw officials hold interest rates steady despite ongoing worries about high and persistent levels of inflation. However, "almost all" policymakers agreed that further hikes would be needed if the economy evolved as they expected, the minutes showed. 

"The staff judged that current vulnerabilities could amplify shocks somewhat more than usual, with elevated asset valuations and leverage at hedge funds representing the most salient vulnerabilities, while strong bank and household balance sheets provided an important buffer against more severe outcomes," the minutes said.

Policymakers expressed concern that huge levels of investment in AI technology could lead to trouble and create broader problems for both the financial system and economy.

"Almost all participants commented on risks associated with a scenario in which the returns on AI investment turned out to be disappointing to investors," the minutes said. "Most participants observed that AI-related debt had grown rapidly and that much of this growth had taken place through complex and opaque financing structures," while "a few" of the unnamed Fed officials were concerned that AI exposure was being concentrated in a "small number" of companies.

Fed officials also cast an anxious eye toward hedge funds.

"Most participants highlighted hedge fund leverage or limited dealer intermediation capacity as potential channels of amplification during periods of market stress," the minutes said.

Fed staff described the financial system as "resilient," with banks having ample access to cash, according to the minutes. But some policymakers worried that "banking system vulnerabilities could emerge rapidly even after seemingly reassuring initial assessments."

Some were also worried the Fed's data on the banking system may miss the full range of exposure some financial firms have.

BUILDING RESILIENCE

Financial markets have been under stress in recent weeks amid questions about the future of AI and how the buildout of the technology has increasingly come to rely on debt. Past periods of financial trouble have been frequently associated with excessive borrowing, and some of those crises have driven the Fed to intervene to stabilize markets.

The latest minutes also showed Fed officials weighing how they can respond to future troubles.

"A few" policymakers mulled boosting banks' capital levels while some also said it is important to better prepare banks to use the Fed's emergency lending discount window facility, which is something officials have been working on for some time.

In addition, "a few" policymakers considered a novel strategy in which the Fed would set up a dedicated method of asset-buying that would explicitly target financial stability concerns.

The Fed is weighing the future of how it uses its balance sheet as a policy tool. Fed holdings have swollen massively over the last two decades due to huge bond purchases during the 2008 global financial crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic.

The pandemic experience has loomed particularly large because bond-buying that began in March 2020 started out as a stabilization tool that morphed into outright stimulus.

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack is among those who would like to see a more clearly defined system for buying bonds that would also entail a strategy to sell them when a crisis has passed. Hammack said earlier this week that any program "should also be temporary, and holdings should be sold in a timely way once market financial stability is restored." 

The minutes noted that "several" policymakers cautioned that monetary policy is not the right tool to deal with market trouble. But the large role now played by AI and technology investment in driving economic growth might complicate that view if large-scale problems emerged.

(Reporting by Michael S. Derby; Editing by Paul Simao)

data.title: Toshiba Releases Photovoltaic-Output Photocoupler for Driving High-Voltage Power MOSFETs in Automotive Equipment
data.description:
– Adjustable turn-off time with an external circuit –

KAWASAKI, Japan--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Toshiba Electronic Devices & Storage Corporation ("Toshiba") has launched “TLX9909,” a photovoltaic-output photocoupler for solid-state relays (SSRs)[1] in automotive equipment. The new product enables adjustment of turn-off time with an external circuit. Volume shipments start today.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261118660977/en/

Relay units for automotive equipment are required to offer a longer service life, smaller sizes and higher reliability. The contacts of mechanical relays are subject to wear and contact failure with long-term use, so mechanical relays are increasingly being replaced by SSRs, which have no moving contacts and use semiconductors for switching.

TLX9909 is a photovoltaic-output photocoupler that directly drives the gate of a discrete MOSFET using electric power generated by a photodiode array[2] when it receives light from the input-side LED. As it does not require an isolated-side power supply or a charge-pump circuit, it helps reduce the number of components and contributes to smaller system size and higher reliability.

Although TLX9909 is configured without a built-in control circuit, it maintains an open voltage[3] of 13.5V (min), equivalent to that of the current TLX9910, which does have a built-in control circuit. By selecting an external gate discharge circuit, users can adjust the turn-off time to suit the connected MOSFET and application, bringing greater flexibility to gate control design. In addition, while the current TLX9905 and TLX9906 offer an open voltage of 7V (min), TLX9909 offers a higher open voltage of 13.5V (min). This makes it easier to secure the gate drive voltage for high-voltage power MOSFETs, expanding the range of MOSFETs that it can be combined with.

Combining TLX9909 with an external high-voltage power MOSFET allows flexible configuration of high-voltage, high-current switching circuits, which can be difficult to achieve with photorelays limited by the ratings of their built-in MOSFETs. The availability of both TLX9909, which emphasizes adjustability through external circuits, and TLX9910, which has a built-in discharge circuit, realizes product selection to meet system requirements, such as flexibility in circuit design and the number of components.

The new product complies with AEC-Q101, the reliability standard for automotive electronic components, and is suitable for SSR applications in automotive equipment such as battery management systems (BMS), on-board chargers (OBC), and inverter units.

In Tokyo, AI- and chip-related shares mostly fell, with Advantest ( ADTTF ) losing 1.88% and Fujikura ( FKURF ) falling 3.9%.

Japan's nonferrous metal index slid to its lowest level in a year as gold prices fell to a 14-month low and copper dropped to its weakest in seven months.

data.title: As criticism mounts, Trump administration says tech outages not coordinated
data.description:
* Clayton cites maintenance and technical changes in outages

* He does not see coordinated or state-sponsored attacks

* Some question official assessment that incidents are unrelated

* String of outages to critical systems started Thursday last week

By Doina Chiacu and Alexandra Alper

WASHINGTON, Nov 18 (Reuters) - The top US intelligence official said on Wednesday the series of disruptions to critical systems over the past week was not a coordinated or state-sponsored attack, as President Donald Trump's administration faces mounting criticism over its response.

Technology-related outages have hit every weekday between Thursday and Tuesday, including a nationwide halt to air travel, a Microsoft ( MSFT ) outage that hit email services and a temporary disruption to the US National Security Agency's network.

The flurry of incidents has raised skepticism among some in the public and in Congress that it was merely a coincidence, as the administration and some cybersecurity experts have said.

"I understand the timing of these incidents can raise questions, and it should. The American people should ask us these questions," Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told a House of Representatives Homeland Security Committee hearing on worldwide threats. "But based on what we know today, after a great deal of diligence, these are separate service outages associated with maintenance and technical changes. They are not a coordinated or state-sponsored attack."

Clayton added that threats from Iran, with which the US is at war, have substantially increased, though he did not link those to the spate of domestic outages.

The administration has struggled at times to give a unified message addressing the growing worries, and some of the Republican president's allies in Washington have demanded more answers about what went wrong.

Though Trump described the situation on Tuesday as "fine," some experts worry that AI tools are feeding a surge of cyberactivity, with cybersecurity companies regularly turning up examples of hackers using AI to launch scores of intrusions at once.

Trump again sought to calm the nation in a Fox News interview in Shenzhen, China, where he is attending the APEC summit of Pacific Rim countries.

"Tell them to relax. Everything's good. These are individual events," Trump said, referring to the American people when interviewer Jacqui Heinrich raised the issue of concerns back home.

QUESTIONS AROUND FLIGHT GROUNDING

At the House hearing, Democratic US Representative Bennie Thompson said it was irresponsible for Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin to board a private jet to attend a college football game last weekend amid the transportation disruptions.

"The so-called leadership of the Trump administration consists of refusing to take responsibility, shifting blame to the others, and putting your own interests above the country," Thompson said.

Mullin defended the administration's handling of the ground stop as "a success" given that thousands of planes landed safely before flights resumed, and said that changing his plans could have led some to worry that he doubted it was safe to fly.

Trump has said he takes no responsibility for the ground stop, which was the longest halt to air travel since the al Qaeda attacks on the United States on September 11, 2001. Officials have said the installation of a router in Arkansas triggered it.

Sherri Graves, a retired speech pathologist from Tennessee, said she viewed the grounding and technology outage with suspicion.

"There's something going on," Graves said. "I'm not sure they know what's going on, the federal government, or if they're sharing it."

SYSTEM UPGRADES

Several House lawmakers asked pointedly how the string of outages could be unrelated.

Republican US Representative Nick LaLota said: "Five (incidents) in one week while we're fighting Iran, while China's getting aggressive, Russia and Ukraine. Does your gut say, 'Just a coincidence.'?"

Clayton replied "it does," in part because agencies and companies are undertaking a "substantial increase" in system upgrades.

Though the upgrades, or patches, are meant in part to address AI-related vulnerabilities, they can also cause disruptions. "When patching at scale, some can cause problems," said Anne Neuberger, general partner at Andreessen Horowitz.

Also in recent days, some JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ) banking activities were disrupted, a United Airlines technology failure delayed about 150 flights and an Apple ( AAPL ) outage affected customer services including iCloud and Apple Pay.

(Additional reporting by Dan Fastenberg in New York and AJ Vicens in Detroit; Writing by Jonathan Spicer; Editing by Scott Malone, Will Dunham and Lincoln Feast.)

data.title: Nvidia retreats as strong outlook fails to dispel uncertainty
data.description:
By Anhata Rooprai and Shashwat Chauhan

Nov 18 (Reuters) - Nvidia ( NVDA ) shares dipped on Wednesday, with analysts more optimistic about future earnings while also more cautious about future stock gains following the AI chip giant's blockbuster forecast and uncertainty caused by CEO Jensen Huang's departure last week.

Nvidia ( NVDA ) shares closed down 2.9%, increasing its loss to 36% from its October 6 record-high close, with much of that drop related to Huang's resignation after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang and two with Nvidia ( NVDA ) employees.

Following Nvidia's ( NVDA ) strong report and outlook, the average analyst estimate for its adjusted net income in its next fiscal year has climbed to $393 billion from $380 billion before Tuesday's late-day report, according to LSEG data.

At the same time, the average analyst price target has dipped to $251.74 from $265.70 on Monday. The stock was last at $152.

The higher earnings estimates and lower price targets show analysts believe Nvidia's ( NVDA ) business remains strong but are applying a more cautious valuation, reflecting risks around the CEO transition and AI spending.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq-100 has shed around $2 trillion in market value so far in November, as investors reassessed lofty AI valuations alongside concerns over China, data center spending and tighter regulation.

"We believe yesterday's results have stabilized sentiment and put a floor under the recent AI selloff, but they have postponed rather than permanently cured investor anxiety," said Neil Shah, vice president of research at Counterpoint.

The next test of the AI trade will come when Anthropic prices its initial public offering later on Wednesday, which could value the frontier lab at up to $1.4 trillion.

Also weighing on shares of Nvidia ( NVDA ) and other AI companies, the Wall Street Journal reported that the US Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating the chipmaker.

The AI trade has also been tested since the Democrats' sweeping midterm wins stoked fears of tougher regulation of data center buildouts, sending the tech-heavy Nasdaq into correction territory earlier this month.

BOARD SAYS NO TO HUANG

Nvidia ( NVDA ) Chairman Harvey Jones ruled out reinstating Huang despite his offer to return. Heidrick & Struggles is leading the search for a permanent CEO among both internal and external candidates.

The stock might struggle to climb further until the company names a permanent CEO and the new leadership shows it can deliver planned products, HSBC analysts said.

Interim CEO Colette Kress has said it was "business as usual," citing customer and supplier support. Nvidia's ( NVDA ) forecast offered evidence that the upheaval has not delayed its product roadmap or weakened demand.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) fourth-quarter revenue forecast beat analysts' estimates, while the company also raised its fiscal 2028 revenue growth outlook to about 75%, saying demand continued to exceed supply.

Third-quarter revenue more than doubled to $115.84 billion, marking a 17th consecutive estimate beat, according to LSEG data.

Adjusted gross margin reached 74.9%. Nvidia ( NVDA ) expects it to bottom between 71% and 72% this quarter as higher supply costs bite, before recovering to between 72% and 73% in fiscal 2028.

"Strong earnings have bought management time," Saxo strategist Charu Chanana said.

CHINA DISAPPEARS FROM OUTLOOK

China contributed $2.4 billion in licensed Hopper data center sales during the quarter, but Nvidia ( NVDA ) assumed no such shipments in its current forecast and said it was no longer shipping those products to the country.

Management said the outlook considered current US export controls, although it was still studying parts of the new rules announced on Monday, while demand elsewhere was expected to absorb the loss of China sales.

"Kress also provided confident answers around Commerce rules, citing that demand is far exceeding supply and that Nvidia ( NVDA ) is studying the rules around the chip delivery to other countries," said Christopher Brown, vice president of investments at Synovus, which holds Nvidia ( NVDA ) shares.

"We just need to understand that demand is not the same as legal ability to ship."

(Reporting by Shashwat Chauhan and Anhata Rooprai in Bengaluru, additional reporting by Avinash P and Noel Randewich; Editing by Joyjeet Das and Nick Zieminski)

data.title: Samsung Electronics downplays concerns about neocloud firms and AI bubble
data.description:
SINGAPORE, Nov 18 (Reuters) - Samsung Electronics ( SSNLF ), the world's top maker of memory chips, on Wednesday downplayed concerns that highly leveraged neocloud providers could fuel a broader AI bubble, saying they account for only a small share of the overall market.

"Neoclouds represent a relatively smaller and limited portion of the overall market, approximately 8%," said Kim Yong-kwan, president and head of corporate management, strategy and operation at Samsung's component business division, at a Morgan Stanley conference in Singapore.

"We do not expect these concerns to pose a significant threat to the broader AI growth trajectory."

Shares of neocloud firms including CoreWeave, which rents out computing capacity to tech firms, have been hit by concerns that their debt-fuelled data center expansions could backfire ​if AI demand slows.

The departure of Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia ( NVDA ) this month could also tighten funding for smaller, highly leveraged neocloud companies that have helped fuel the industry's rapid expansion, analysts and investors have said.

Kang Suk-chae, Samsung's Head of Foundry Sales & Marketing, said the current AI investment boom was structural rather than cyclical, with long-term contracts between chipmakers and customers providing greater visibility over demand and supply.

He said the current boom differed from previous cycles in which speculative investment ultimately led to overcapacity.

"In short, today's investment is not a result of speculation, but actual tangible demand," Kang said, saying the ongoing chip shortage would "persist for the foreseeable future."

He said Samsung's foundry business, which competes with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, has diversified manufacturing footprints "to mitigate supply chains" and offers "a one-stop solution" that includes memory and advanced packaging.

Kim reiterated Samsung's previous statement that it would carry out its remaining shareholder returns through a mix of cash dividends and a "substantial" share repurchase and cancellation program.

He said the company had a number of factors to consider, including capital expenditures, before announcing details on its shareholder return package in January.

'Yalta'? Hmmmm

Suggestions that the trilateral meeting on Thursday between the leaders of China, the US and Russia could be compared to the 1945 Yalta Conference always seemed a bit far-fetched. Expectations for a major breakthrough on issues of substance, like security or trade, should probably be dialed down.

That said, it is historic - it is the first face-to-face meeting among the heads of state of China, Russia, and the US. So, it is a good photo opportunity, and a chance to pledge ongoing dialogue, cooperation and mutual respect. Xi seemed to be showing Trump significant respect, breaking with protocol to meet him at the airport. This gesture wasn't afforded to the Russian leader, however.

Inflated expectations

The longer inflation is above target, usually 2%, the more likely consumers and business expect it to stay there. This risks a widespread loss of faith in policymakers whose job it is to keep a lid on prices, fueling central bank credibility issues that can have serious spillover effects for financial markets. These are problems officials in the US and UK are grappling with.

On Wednesday, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said the Fed might need more aggressive action to remind people that "3% is not the inflation number you should be thinking about going forward." Meanwhile, figures on Wednesday showed that UK inflation rose to 3.6% in October, the highest in a year. Indeed, Britain is facing its longest run without inflation dipping below 2% since the early 1990s.
